title: The migration process — backfill vs live

text.insert: The migration map records the disposition and rebuild path for each legacy knowledge source. Its opening table provides the source-by-source mapping, followed by decisions that govern runtime integration and backfill behavior.
The crosswalk has no code counterpart today (zero references in
). It stays a generated data table under
; a small resolver in the server's boot-injection assembly maps target path → wiki page titles at prompt-build time, and
folds into it there. No graph builder — the connection map draws the crosswalk as a dashed runtime query path, not a build-time edge, and the corpus stays out of the graph.
row: the corpus stays the file mirror under
, searched by worker-side tooling. No server component, no index service — raw text searched at need is the corpus regime working as designed, with nothing to drift.

The deprecated-trio verdict is amended for discord: instead of 'leave', the discord archive becomes a scheduled-extraction source — a daily cron mines it into proposed learnings with message-level evidence refs (see the sources catalog). Workers still never search it directly. Data sheet and mirrors remain left/retired.

verdict changes from 'keep as docs + seed' to 'docs only': the seed import is dropped (no evidence refs — see the retired-sources decision). The knowledge it encoded will be re-derived by the extraction pipeline with evidence.

The knowledge base is rebuilt from scratch under the new semantics: every source — the discord archive, all past PRs, worker transcripts and logs — is reprocessed through the librarian intake. The per-source rebuild process (extractor, batching, ordering) gets detailed here, row by row, as each is designed.
The migration process — backfill vs live

The backfill is not a different agent — it is the same librarian running a different range. Live flow processes items as they arrive, anchoring against the up-to-date checkout while the harness runs, resolving conflicts as new information contradicts existing learnings. Backfill runs the identical pipeline from the beginning of each source. The one structural difference: backfill is present-anchored — it does not replay history as a naive reader. Statements anchor against today's code first; chronology enters only as timestamps on evidence.
